_help: A written scene: the story without the AI. A scene is made of parts, and start says which part comes first. Each part has text, which the player reads, and choices, which lead to other parts. Restart the game after changing this file, and run npm test to have it checked.

text is a list of paragraphs, in the same format the game master writes: @Name: "words" for speech, > is never needed here because choices are listed below, and a line starting => is a consequence the player sees boxed.

A choice has say (its words), and either to (the part it leads to) or check (a skill and difficulty, like persuasion:moderate, with a person's id after a second colon when they're the one being talked to) with pass and fail. tags are shown before the words: +Voss or -Tarrow for someone who'd approve or disapprove, mercy or iron and the other beliefs, and ! for a warning.

A part can also have do: things that happen when it begins, each with tool and the same fields the AI uses (see src/tools.js), such as add_journal, note_contact, update_quest, change_credits or shift_ideology. note is a game message shown with the part. check on a part opens a check the story demands, with reason, pass and fail. fight on a part starts a fight, with the same fields as start_combat, and won, lost, and if you like fled, gaveUp and talked. end: true closes the scene.
A scene called opening_<life> opens the story for that life (the ids are in starts.json), opening fits anyone else, and thread_<story> plays when a story from the Leads menu is taken up.
title: A Light on Every Band

text: The bridge is cold enough to see your breath, and nobody has said the word captain yet. The last one is three hours dead, and the chair still has his thumb worn into the armrest.
Forty-one green dots sit on the plot table. One of them flickers.
@Lieutenant Iven Sorel: "It's still there, Captain." He says it low, as if someone's asleep nearby. "Every band. Six seconds, then it starts again. It isn't noise. I'd know noise."

@Commander Ilya Voss: "Captain." She says it as if she hasn't finished deciding. "Two weeks of fuel. Three of food, if nobody eats much. The Choir will find our slowest ship in a few days, the way they always do. And half the fleet is already calling that signal a harbor." She lets that sit. "Your orders."

choices.say: Ask her what she'd do, if the chair were hers
Ask what she isn't telling you
Tell the fleet the truth: you don't know what the signal is yet
Say nothing, and listen to it

text: She doesn't look at the chair. She looks at the dots.

@Commander Ilya Voss: "Keep them together. Find out what that signal is before I point thirty thousand people at it. Haven Station is one jump, and there's a man there who can read a signal that old, if he's still alive and still sober." A pause. "You asked. Most wouldn't have."
=> Voss will remember that you asked her first.

do.name: Ilya Voss
do.note: You asked for her judgment before you gave your first order.

do.entry: Voss's advice on day one: keep the fleet together, and find out what the signal is before leading anyone toward it. There's a man at Haven Station who can read old signals.

text: Something in her jaw moves, where the scar is.

@Commander Ilya Voss: "Fine. I have a list. Which ships can't keep up, and the day we stop trying to make them. I wrote it last night, before anyone asked me to." She meets your eye. "You'll want one of your own, Captain. You'll hate having it."
=> Voss told you about her list.

do.entry: Voss keeps a list: the ships the fleet can't keep up with, and the day she'd stop trying. She made it before anyone asked.

do.reason: You got the truth out of Voss

text: @Commander Ilya Voss: "Captain. If I had something to tell you, you'd have it." The scar along her jaw doesn't move at all. "Orders."
Behind her, Sorel finds something very interesting in his headset.
@Lieutenant Iven Sorel: "Fleet-wide, Captain. Say again when you're ready. Over."

You tell forty-one ships that you don't know what the signal is, that nobody does yet, and that you're going to find out before you take them anywhere. The channel stays open a second too long afterward, and you can hear the quiet on the Sundial.
@Commander Ilya Voss: "Well." It's almost approval. "Now they know."
=> The whole fleet heard you say you don't know.

do.reason: You told the fleet the truth instead of a hope
The fleet heard the truth from you

do.entry: Your first words to the fleet were that you don't know what the signal is yet, and that you'd find out before taking them anywhere.

text: Sorel puts it on the bridge speakers without being asked. Six seconds. A tone under static, then something that might be a voice, then the tone again.
@Ensign Lira Vey: "Confirming: the same six seconds, forty times since the watch began. The arm is elevated. Please disregard the arm."
@Ensign Pell Asante: "It's, it's pretty, is the thing. Captain." She catches herself a beat late, as always.
Nobody on the bridge says the word home, and everyone has heard it.

do.entry: The signal: six seconds, a tone under static, and something like a voice. The bridge hears a word in it that nobody will say out loud.

text: Voss waits. The dots on the table don't.
@Commander Ilya Voss: "Haven Station is one jump. The council will want to be told before we go, and Speaker Halm will want to be told twice. I can have Pell plot it while you decide."
The bridge goes back to work around you, the way a bridge does when it's decided to trust you for an hour.

choices.say: Have Pell plot the course for Haven
Go and see the ship first

text: @Ensign Pell Asante: "Plotted, sir. Captain. One jump, about sixteen hours, and we'd come out with fuel to spare." A breath. "Not a lot to spare."
=> The course to Haven Station is laid in. Set it from the Star map when you're ready.
That's the end of the written opening. You can walk the ship, talk to the crew about what they've heard, and go to Haven from the Star map.

do.objective: Haven Station is plotted. Set course from the Star map when you're ready, and tell the council first if you want Speaker Halm on your side.

text: You leave the chair empty a while longer. Nobody says anything about it, and Voss goes back to her list.
That's the end of the written opening. You can walk the ship, talk to the crew about what they've heard, and go to Haven from the Star map.

do.objective: Haven Station is one jump away. Set course from the Star map when you're ready, and tell the council first if you want Speaker Halm on your side.
